initial_presentation: A 41-year-old Chinese male was admitted to the Second Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University, China, on 9 August 2015, due to a progressively unstable gait over the past 4 years. The patient reported experiencing an unstable gait, leg weakness, and involuntary forward bending of both knees starting at age 37, which had progressively worsened. During childhood, the patient exhibited involuntary limb twisting and poor movement. Over the past 2 years, he experienced a decline in memory and slow reactions, leading to an inability to work. The patient denied any history of other chronic diseases or similar family history. Upon admission, physical examination showed no change in limb muscle tone. Hoffman’s sign, Romberg sign, finger-to-nose test, and bilateral Babinski sign were negative. The patient exhibited slow alternate motions and decreased tendon reflexes in all four limbs. Muscle strength in all four limbs was graded as five.

A 64-year-old woman presented with mildly itchy brownish to red rashes on both lateral malleoli for 7 months. She had previously been treated for lichen simplex chronicus with various topical steroids, including 0.05% clobetasol propionate ointment and triamcinolone acetonide 10 mg/mL injection, but showed minimal improvement. There was no history of significant weight loss or trauma to the affected area. She was otherwise in good health. Physical examination showed bilateral well-defined brownish hyperkeratotic plaques with a red rim on both lateral malleoli. The scalp and nails were normal, and other physical examinations were unremarkable.
A 42-year-old female with a history of borderline hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus underwent elective endometrial ablation for treatment of menorrhagia.

A 72-year-old right-handed woman with 12 years of education began experiencing word-finding difficulties, characterized by prolonged pauses and frequent use of pronouns. She also reported challenges in writing Chinese characters due to their complexity. At age 75, she visited Edogawa Hospital. Neurological examinations were normal, with no signs of parkinsonism. Initial linguistic assessment revealed fluent speech with circumlocutory patterns and occasional lexical paraphasias. She could repeat single words but had difficulty repeating sentences. Her forward digit span was up to five digits. Comprehension of single words, both spoken and written, was intact, but comprehension of complex sentences was sometimes impaired. Writing skills were poor, marked by phonological paragraphias and difficulty remembering Chinese characters. Despite these linguistic issues, she maintained an independent lifestyle, had no significant episodic memory problems, and never became lost. She was aware of her condition.

A 73-year-old woman experienced intense pain in the right scapular region, rated 8.9 out of 10 on the numerical rating scale. This severe pain persisted for one week before gradually decreasing in intensity. Three weeks after the initial onset of symptoms, she encountered difficulty raising her right arm and was unable to comb her hair or wash her face. Physical examination revealed 2/5 strength in the right shoulder abductor and flexor muscles, and 4/5 strength in the right elbow flexor muscle. Sensation to pin prick was equal in both upper extremities. Deep tendon reflexes were absent in the right biceps brachii and right triceps brachii.

A 17-year-old male presented with multiple papules and nodules with necrosis on the trunk and limbs, persisting for one month. Initially, no visible red papules or nodules were present on the torso and limbs. Over time, papules and nodules measuring 0.8×0.4 cm appeared, increased in number, developed ulcerated, crusted surfaces, and were slightly itchy but painless.

A ten-year-old boy presented with complaints of nasal regurgitation during eating and a desire for facial aesthetic correction. The family history was negative for cleft lip and palate. According to his mother, the patient was born after a full-term pregnancy without complications, and there was no history of maternal medication or illness during pregnancy. The patient had previously undergone repair of bilateral cleft lip at ten months old. Extraoral examination showed the premaxilla and maxillary central incisors hanging down, resulting in an unaesthetic appearance. The lower lip exhibited bilateral, paramedian small pits. Intraoral soft tissue examination revealed bilateral alveolar clefts in the premaxillary region. The maxillary arch was constricted with a high arched palate. The patient had mixed dentition with congenitally missing bilateral maxillary lateral incisors. Additionally, the patient reported recurrent respiratory tract infections, breathlessness, regurgitation of food, and a nasal twang during speech.

A 20-year-old male experienced cough, rhinorrhea, wheezing, and dyspnea after exposure to rainy conditions. He had a history of childhood asthma and a family history of asthma, including his mother and three elder sisters. After treatment with inhaled corticosteroids, his symptoms improved over three days. Nine days later, he developed an unsteady gait. By day 3, he experienced blurred vision, dizziness, and nausea. On day 12, he became intermittently drowsy but could be aroused by noxious stimulation. On day 18, he had a tonic-clonic seizure, prompting a neurological evaluation. Neurological examination revealed full consciousness, a wide-based gait, and an inability to stand on one foot. There were limitations in lateral gaze in the left eye and vertical gaze in both eyes, while motor and sensory functions were intact.
A 2-year-old Brazilian boy, born to non-consanguineous parents, exhibited persistent violaceous skin lesions and recurrent fever starting at 10 days old.

A 56-year-old woman presented with an incidental left renal mass discovered during an evaluation for hypertension. She measured 167 cm in height and weighed 52 kg. Her blood pressure was 166/102 mmHg, and her heart rate was 116 bpm. She had a history of uncontrolled hypertension and was taking amlodipine 10 mg once daily. She reported a slight headache. Physical examination revealed significant ascites. General blood chemistry tests and blood counts were normal. Serum catecholamine levels were elevated: adrenaline at 148 pg/mL (normal 0–100 pg/mL), noradrenaline at 902 pg/mL (normal 100–450 pg/mL), and dopamine at 28 pg/mL (normal 0–20 pg/mL). A 24-hour urine collection showed adrenaline at 13.6 μg/day (normal 3.4–26.9 μg/day), noradrenaline at 250.6 μg/day (normal 48.6–168.4 μg/day), and dopamine at 1146 μg/day (normal 365–961.5 μg/day).
